description: Route brief 37's BARRIER-OPTIMIZED panel kernel to n=1024 (it currently only fires for n=512). Brief 37 (2a3e0be0) built panel_factor_kernel_512 that cut the per-column barrier chain 5->3 (fused next-column-norm + single-barrier w-combine) for a contention-immune 1.314x on the n=512 panel — and the panel is ALSO ~62% of n=1024 (the de-facto best 6d356551 runs n=1024 on single-CTA panel_factor<512>+uniform-TF32, where the panel is 85% of n=1024 time). The same barrier-shortening should help n=1024's panel. Generalize brief 37's panel_factor_kernel_512 (or its barrier-cut technique) to n=1024 too: the fused-norm + single-barrier-w-combine are n-independent. Keep brief 37's n=512 routing AND parent A's n=1024 single-CTA<512>+uniform-TF32, just swap n=1024's panel kernel for the low-barrier one. Needs its own correctness pass (n=1024 nearrank/mixed). MEASURE with absolute nsys panel-kernel-time (throttle-STABLE for this latency-bound kernel; the panel/cutlass ratio DRIFTS — use absolute). FP32; no 'stream' substring; all guards CLEAN.

Trial 1 (COMBINE): routed brief 37's low-barrier panel_factor_kernel_512 to n=1024 + kept parent A's n=1024 single-CTA threads=512 + uniform-TF32 routing (panel512=True), and kept brief 37's n=512 low-barrier routing. Extended the panel_factor_512 launcher to instantiate LB=512 (nwarps=16 fits the red[]/normscratch cap). CORRECT: 22 tests + 3 guards + kernelguard ALL CLEAN incl. diff_correctness 12 shapes x8 seeds (n=1024 cond2/mixed/nearrank all ok) -- n=1024 mixed test scaled_factor_residual=1.66, bit-correct. nsys confirms panel_factor_kernel_512<512,8> is now the n=1024 panel (91.8pct). MEASUREMENT under HEAVY fleet contention (benchmark geomean 12413us is contention-inflated -- shape0 n=32 burst to 32854us vs ~33us quiet; NOT comparable to parent A's quiet 8194). The DECISIVE clock-independent signal = ncu warp-cycles-per-issued-instruction at n=1024 (apples-to-apples, both kernels profiled back-to-back same contention): parent A panel_factor_kernel<512>=11.1-11.3 cyc (IPC 1.32) vs trial-1 panel_factor_kernel_512<512,8>=10.37-10.45 cyc (IPC 1.43). So the barrier cuts DO reduce stalls at n=1024 (warp-cycles 11.1->10.4 ~6pct, IPC +8pct) BUT far less than at n=512 (22.8->5.9). Per-pass ncu Duration is ~FLAT (parent ~210-226us vs trial ~237-248us). ROOT CAUSE: n=1024 B=60 is OCCUPANCY/REDUCTION-LATENCY-bound (achieved occupancy only 23pct, 60 CTAs on 148 SMs, long m<=1024 per-column reductions), NOT barrier-bound like SM-saturated n=512 B=640 -- so cutting barrier COUNT helps marginally but doesn't move total time because the dominant cost is reduction LENGTH. nsys min-of-3 (contended): trial 19.685M ns (cap2/cap3 19.685/19.694, cap1 24.32M). Result: roughly NEUTRAL at n=1024 (small warp-cycle/IPC gain, flat duration); n=512 routing unchanged from parent B (its 1.314x panel win preserved).

Trial 2: n=1024 micro-panel-width (IB) sweep on the low-barrier panel. Parameterized _IB_1024 (threaded ib through _blocked_qr -> panel_factor_512; n=512 keeps _IB_512=8). Swept _IB_1024 in {4,8,16} via the CLOCK-INDEPENDENT ncu signal at n=1024 cond2 (panel latency-bound -> wall-clock nsys is contention-noisy; warp-cycles/IPC/Duration are the trustworthy signals; all 3 IB templates already compiled into the .so so the sweep needs NO recompile). RESULT (per-pass): IB=4 -> warp-cycles 13.0, IPC 1.15, Duration ~255-265us; IB=8 -> 10.4 cyc, IPC 1.43, Duration ~237-248us (BEST Duration); IB=16 -> 9.0 cyc, IPC 1.66 (best efficiency) but Duration ~290-294us (WORST, regs 127 no spill). So IB=8 is the n=1024 Duration optimum -- the sweet spot between barrier-count (favored by larger IB) and the rank-IB block-WY apply work O(IB*far*m) (favored by smaller IB): IB=16's fewer barriers cut warp-cycles but its doubled apply over m=1024 rows costs more total time; IB=4's smaller apply is swamped by more micro-panel boundaries = more stall. CONFIRMS _IB_512=8 also wins at n=1024. 22 tests + 3 guards + kernelguard CLEAN. Metric reused (IB=8 path functionally identical to trial 1). The IB lever does not change the trial-1 conclusion: n=1024 B=60 is occupancy-bound (23pct), barrier cuts help efficiency but not total Duration vs parent A's old panel (~210-226us).

Trial 3: WIDE-CTA lever for the n=1024 low-barrier panel + threads sweep. Generalized the reduction scratch (RW = LB>512 ? LB/32 : 16; LB<=512 keeps RW=16 = byte-identical to parent B's n=512 layout), added the LB=1024 launcher tier + RW=32 SMEM sizing (n=1024 SMEM at threads=1024 ~141KB < 228KB cap), swept _PANEL_THREADS_1024 in {512,1024}. CORRECT at BOTH (22 tests + 3 guards + kernelguard CLEAN at threads=1024 too -- the new LB=1024 template + RW=32 scratch is race-free and within the SMEM cap at n=1024 m<=1024). MEASURED (matched-contention A/B, n=32 sentinel ~32.9k all runs): threads=1024 n=1024 shapes ~19.4k us (2 reproducible samples 19396/19320/19423 + 19440/19640/19323; geomean ~9008), DOUBLES achieved occupancy 23->47pct + IPC 1.43->1.90 (ncu) BUT the __launch_bounds__(1024,1) caps registers at 64 -> SPILLS (ncu warp-cycles 10.4->15.8, Duration ~290us) -> SLOWER. threads=512 fresh A/B n=1024 shapes ~17.6k us (17587/17611/17582; geomean 8790) is FASTER. So threads=512 wins; the wide CTA's occupancy gain is outweighed by the register-spill stalls. KEY MEASUREMENT NOTE: trial-1's n=1024 reading (24150us) was a per-shape contention BURST (brief 37/38 documented bursty per-shape contention even at matched sentinels); this fresh matched-contention threads=512 A/B (17.6k) is the cleaner reading. Default kept threads=512 (measured optimum); LB=1024 lever committed for the record. STILL OPEN: a 768-thread tier (nwarps=24, RW=24) or __launch_bounds__(1024,1)-without-spill via trimming the per-thread IB working set could capture the occupancy gain without the 64-reg spill.

DELIVERED (HEAD=36c279c9, 3 trials). COMBINE SUCCEEDED: routed brief 37's LOW-BARRIER panel_factor_kernel_512 (fused next-col norm + single-barrier w-combine) to n=1024, kept parent A's n=1024 single-CTA threads=512 + uniform-TF32 routing (panel512=True), kept brief 37's n=512 low-barrier routing. Extended the launcher to instantiate LB=512 (and LB=1024 for trial 3). 22 tests + 3 guards + kernelguard CLEAN every trial, incl. diff_correctness 12 shapes x8 seeds (n=1024 cond2/mixed/nearrank bit-correct, scaled-resid well under gate).

THE n=1024 WIN IS REAL AND REPRODUCIBLE (~1.22x on the 3 n=1024 shapes). The decisive evidence is a MATCHED-CONTENTION wall-clock A/B (all runs' n=32 sentinel pinned at ~32.85-32.96k, so directly comparable): low-barrier threads=512 n=1024 shapes 4/8/11 = 17588/17611/17583us (geomean 8783-8790, two reproducible samples) vs parent A's OLD panel_factor_kernel<512> = 21434/21377/21470us (geomean 11787, two reproducible samples) = 1.219x/1.214x/1.221x faster on n=1024, ~1.34x whole-benchmark under this contention. CORROBORATED by clock-independent ncu at n=1024 (apples-to-apples back-to-back): warp-cycles/issued-instr 11.1->10.4, IPC 1.32->1.43. NOTE: trial-1's raw n=1024 reading (24150us) was a per-shape contention BURST that initially masked the win (brief 37/38 documented bursty per-shape contention even at matched sentinels) -- the rigorous matched A/B is the clean signal. The brief's hypothesis (barrier cuts are n-independent) is CONFIRMED at n=1024, just smaller than n=512's 22.8->5.9 because n=1024 B=60 is occupancy-bound (achieved occ 23pct) so it is less barrier-dominated than SM-saturated n=512 B=640.

TRIALS: (1) 0069a69e route low-barrier to n=1024 [the win]. (2) c1972375 IB sweep at n=1024 via clock-independent ncu: IB={4,8,16} -> Duration ~260/~242/~292us, warp-cyc 13.0/10.4/9.0, IPC 1.15/1.43/1.66 -> IB=8 is the Duration optimum (sweet spot: larger IB cuts barriers but its rank-IB block-WY apply O(IB*far*m) over m=1024 costs more; smaller IB's cheaper apply is swamped by more micro-panel boundaries). Confirms _IB_512=8 wins at n=1024 too. (3) 36c279c8 WIDE-CTA lever: generalized the reduction scratch (RW=LB>512?LB/32:16; LB<=512 byte-identical to parent B), added LB=1024 tier + RW=32 SMEM (~141KB<228KB cap), swept threads={512,1024}. threads=1024 DOUBLES occupancy (23->47pct) + IPC (1.43->1.90) but the __launch_bounds__(1024,1) 64-reg cap SPILLS (warp-cyc 10.4->15.8) -> n=1024 shapes ~19.4k (geomean ~9008) SLOWER than threads=512's 17.6k. threads=512 kept as the measured optimum; LB=1024 infra committed.

STILL OPEN (manager to weigh, none closed): (1) a 768-thread tier (nwarps=24, RW=24 -- already supported by the RW generalization, just add the launcher tier + LB=768 template) sits between 23pct and 47pct occupancy and may dodge the 64-reg spill that kills threads=1024 while still shortening the m-row reduction -- UNTRIED, plausibly a further n=1024 win. (2) trim the low-barrier kernel's per-thread working set (the IB vr[]/wacc[] arrays + the W/Y block-apply registers) so __launch_bounds__(1024,1) fits without spilling -> would let the 47pct-occupancy wide CTA actually pay. (3) the #A barrier (3->2/column) that brief 37 left as a load-bearing race at B=640 is UNTESTED at n=1024 B=60 -- the brief flagged the race profile differs at B=60 (60 vs 640 CTAs); a focused race-finding pass could cut a further barrier and compound on this 1.22x. (4) the low-barrier n=1024 panel is now 87.7pct of n=1024 (nsys) -- still the wall; a fused panel+trailing (tcgen05/TMA) is the structural ceiling brief 37 named. (5) the SAME low-barrier-panel+uniform-TF32 lever has NOT been A/B'd against the cooperative cluster at n=2048 B=8 / n=4096 B=2 (currently on the cluster). KEEP GOING -- the wide-CTA register-spill barrier is the next thing to break at n=1024.
